chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Salama, from Harun ibn Kharaja, from Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The prayer in the Sacred Masjid is equivalent to one hundred thousand prayers.

key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ: The Sacred Masjid (specifically Al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for prayer in the Sacred Masjid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via a chain of reliable transmitters, emphasizing the immense spiritual reward of the Sacred Mosque. While some scholars discuss whether this 'one hundred thousand' is literal or symbolic, the hadith underscores the unique sanctity of the Kaaba as the qibla and the focal point of global worship. This merit is often contrasted with the reward of Medina, highlighting the distinct hierarchical status of the two holiest sites in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Salma, from Haroun Bin Kharjat, from Samit, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Salaat in the Sacred Masjid equates to one hundred thousand Salaats (elsewhere)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn abu Salmah from Flarun ibn Kharijah from Samet who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his ancestors, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, who have said that
performing Salat (prayer) in Masjid al-Haram is equal to one hundred thousand Salat (prayer) elsewhere.”
